Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the performance/SLO and network items we discussed for the private (VPC/on-prem) deployment: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Target P95 latency for streaming completions: <= 150ms token-to-token for single-turn inference.
- Target steady-state throughput: ~800 tokens/sec across 10 concurrent streams.
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent requests during peak (mix of streaming and non-streaming).
- Streaming requirements: chunked client-side consumption with server-side keep-alive and immediate token push.
- Network constraints: requests will originate from Acme VPC over AWS Transit Gateway to Redwood-managed peering; expected RTT budget <= 25ms one-way if possible.

Open questions / asks from Redwood
1) Can you share the network path diagram (VPN/peering) and egress IP ranges for the test subnets? (we attached a sample network-diagram template)
2) Are there any internal firewalls/proxies doing TCP termination or deep packet inspection we should be aware of?
3) Expected TLS termination point (Acme edge vs. Redwood edge)? This affects TCP/TLS handshake overhead in our latency budget.
4) Any strict SOC/retention behaviour that would affect streaming sessions (e.g., forced session rekeying)?

Proposed next steps
- Acme: drop the completed network diagram + egress ranges into the Drive link (or reply to this thread).
- Redwood (Aditya): run a quick latency/handshake test matrix once we have egress IPs and preferred TLS termination point.
- Redwood (Marissa): provide an initial SLO sheet (attached slo-requirements.xlsx) and suggested canary plan for a private rollout.

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (template), slo-requirements.xlsx (initial SLOs & test plan)

If this summary looks right I can schedule a follow-up technical sync with Aditya and your networking team tomorrow (30 mins).

Thanks,

Alex / Marissa — thanks, this is great context. A few technical clarifications ahead of the sync so we can be prepared to validate: 

Latency and handshake budget
- If TLS terminates at your edge LB (F5), can you confirm whether we will see the client TCP/TLS handshake complete before we receive the request at Redwood? If not, we should plan for an extra 40-80ms on first-byte for short-lived connections.

Keep-alive and connection reuse
- Do you have long-lived keep-alive settings between your LB and downstream peers? Persistent connections with idle timeout >= 60s will help us meet P95 targets under load.

Path MTU / jumbo frames
- Does your network allow jumbo frames on the Transit Gateway/direct path? Larger MTU reduces segmentation overhead for large response payloads (embeddings / batch completions).

Traffic shaping and egress/throttling
- Any per-source IP or per-subnet shaping we should be aware of? If you have an enforced egress rate limit, please share the policy.

Test plan outline (what we'll run in the sync)
1) TLS handshake RTT matrix from multiple test agents inside your VPC to the proposed peering IPs.
2) Sustained concurrency ramp to 50 concurrent sessions (mix of streaming and non-streaming) and a short burst test to 200 concurrent for 60s.
3) Token-level loopback measurement for streaming latency (client->server token push -> first token and inter-token gaps).

If you can share the egress ranges and the LB behavior we can prepare the test agents and a small load script. Also please upload the completed network diagram to the Drive link Marissa provided.

Cheers,
